To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the turnover of newly synthesized protein in the myocyte of the aortic media, as visualized by quantitative radioautography, is characterized by a sedentary component, which persists throughout life, and by a secretory component, which is important during development and is maintained to a lesser degree in the adult animal.

1) the myocyte has a secretory activity that persists into maturity; 2) the sedentary protein of the myocyte turns over at the same rate in both the adult and young animal; 3) the exportable protein of the myoplsm turns over at different rates in the adult and young myocyte; 4) the turnover of exportable protein is related to the synthesis of elastin; 5) the turnover of the myoplasic protein is not related

the turnover of newly formed protein in the myoplasm of the adult and immature myocyte is similar in the thoracic and the abdominal aorta, but that turnover of exportable protein varies with age and location in the aorta.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the myocyte in the tunica media of the aorta.
the study of the myocyte as a dynamic cell and with the possible role of its protein metabolism in aortic pathology.
the study of the protein turnover in the aortic tunical myocyte of the adult and the young animal, as visualized by light and electron microscopic quantitative radioautography.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, as a result of the radioautographic studies, the myocyte of the adult aorta is characterized by a low turnover of its protein constituents and by a low secretory activity.
the myocyte of the adult aortic tunica intima and media has a high turnover rate of proteins, both exportable and sedimentary.
the myocyte of the aortic wall is an active cell with a high rate of protein turnover, and that this activity is not limited to any specific segment of the aorta.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the myocyte, in its post-natal growth phase, synthesizes a large amount of protein, some of which is exported.
in the adult myocyte the turnover of secretory proteins is similar to that of sedentary proteins.
the myocyte, as a secretory cell, maintains its ability to synthesize proteins and to secrete them throughout life.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the myocyte of the mature mouse is not a sedentary, non-proliferative cell.
the myocyte is not a quiescent cell, but rather a dynamic one.

, in the mature myocytes, there is a constant renewal of the cytoplasmic matrix and of the contractile apparatus, which are probably involved in the maintenance of the contractile properties of the myocytes.
